# CHAPTER 24
# UNIFORM CONVERGENCE AND POWER SERIES
blocks.translation:
# 第 24 章
# 一致收敛与幂级数

blocks.source: The considerations at the end of the previous chapter suggest an entirely new way of looking at infinite series. Our attention will shift from particular infinite sums to equations like
blocks.translation: 上一章末尾的讨论，提出了一种看待无穷级数的全新方式。我们的注意力将从某个具体的无穷和，转向下面这样的等式：

blocks.source: which concern sums of quantities that depend on $x$. In other words, we are interested in *functions* defined by equations of the form
blocks.translation: 这里求和的各个量依赖于 $x$。换句话说，我们关心的是由下列形式的等式定义的*函数*：

blocks.source: (in the previous example $f_n(x)=x^{n-1}/(n-1)!$). In such a situation $\{f_n\}$ will be some sequence of functions; for each $x$ we obtain a sequence of numbers $\{f_n(x)\}$, and $f(x)$ is the sum of this sequence. In order to analyze such functions it will certainly be necessary to remember that each sum
blocks.translation: （在前面的例子中，$f_n(x)=x^{n-1}/(n-1)!$）。在这种情况下，$\{f_n\}$ 是某个函数列；对于每个 $x$，我们得到一个数列 $\{f_n(x)\}$，而 $f(x)$ 就是这个数列的和。要分析这样的函数，当然必须记住，每个和

blocks.source: is, by definition, the limit of the sequence
blocks.translation: 按定义都是下面这个数列的极限：

blocks.source: If we define a new sequence of functions $\{s_n\}$ by
blocks.translation: 如果用下式定义一个新的函数列 $\{s_n\}$：

blocks.source: $$s_n=f_1+\cdots+f_n,$$
then we can express this fact more succinctly by writing
blocks.translation: 那么，我们就可以把这个事实更简洁地写成

blocks.source: $$f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}s_n(x).$$
For some time we shall therefore concentrate on functions defined as limits,
blocks.translation: 因此，接下来一段时间，我们将集中研究通过极限定义的函数，

blocks.source: $$f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x),$$

rather than on functions defined as infinite sums. The total body of results about such functions can be summed up very easily: nothing one would hope to be true actually is—instead we have a splendid collection of counterexamples. The first of these shows that even if each $f_n$ is continuous, the function $f$ may not be! Contrary to what you may expect, the functions $f_n$ will be very simple. Figure 1 shows the graphs of the functions
blocks.translation: 而不是通过无穷和定义的函数。关于这类函数的全部结果，很容易概括：我们希望成立的事情，一件也没有真的成立——取而代之的是一批精彩的反例。第一个反例表明，即使每个 $f_n$ 都连续，函数 $f$ 也可能不连续！与你可能预想的相反，函数 $f_n$ 将非常简单。图 1 展示了下列函数的图像：

blocks.source: $$f_n(x)=\begin{cases}x^n,&0\le x\le1\\1,&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$
These functions are all continuous, but the function $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ is not continuous; in fact,
blocks.translation: 这些函数全都连续，但函数 $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ 并不连续；事实上，

blocks.source: $$\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=\begin{cases}0,&0\le x<1\\1,&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$
Another example of this same phenomenon is illustrated in Figure 2; the functions $f_n$ are defined by
blocks.translation: 图 2 展示了同一现象的另一个例子；函数 $f_n$ 定义为

blocks.source: $$f_n(x)=\begin{cases}-1,&x\le-\dfrac1n\\nx,&-\dfrac1n\le x\le\dfrac1n\\1,&\dfrac1n\le x.\end{cases}$$
In this case, if $x<0$, then $f_n(x)$ is eventually (i.e., for large enough $n$) equal to $-1$, and if $x>0$, then $f_n(x)$ is eventually $1$, while $f_n(0)=0$ for all $n$. Thus
blocks.translation: 在这个例子中，如果 $x<0$，那么 $f_n(x)$ 最终（即对于充分大的 $n$）等于 $-1$；如果 $x>0$，那么 $f_n(x)$ 最终等于 $1$；而对于所有 $n$，都有 $f_n(0)=0$。因此

blocks.source: $$\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=\begin{cases}-1,&x<0\\0,&x=0\\1,&x>0;\end{cases}$$
so, once again, the function $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ is not continuous.
blocks.translation: 所以，函数 $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ 再次不连续。

blocks.source: By rounding off the corners in the previous examples it is even possible to produce a sequence of *differentiable* functions $\{f_n\}$ for which the function $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ is not continuous. One such sequence is easy to define explicitly:
blocks.translation: 把前面例子中的拐角磨圆，甚至可以构造出一个*可导*函数列 $\{f_n\}$，而函数 $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ 仍不连续。其中一个这样的函数列很容易显式定义：

blocks.source: $$f_n(x)=\begin{cases}-1,&x\le-\dfrac1n\\\sin\dfrac{n\pi x}{2},&-\dfrac1n\le x\le\dfrac1n\\1,&\dfrac1n\le x.\end{cases}$$
These functions are differentiable (Figure 3), but we still have
blocks.translation: 这些函数可导（图 3），但我们仍然有

blocks.source: $$\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=\begin{cases}-1,&x<0\\0,&x=0\\1,&x>0.\end{cases}$$

Continuity and differentiability are, moreover, not the only properties for which problems arise. Another difficulty is illustrated by the sequence $\{f_n\}$ shown in Figure 4; on the interval $[0,1/n]$ the graph of $f_n$ forms an isosceles triangle of altitude $n$, while $f_n(x)=0$ for $x\ge1/n$. These functions may be defined explicitly as follows:
blocks.translation: 此外，连续性和可导性并不是唯一会出问题的性质。图 4 中的函数列 $\{f_n\}$ 展示了另一种困难；在区间 $[0,1/n]$ 上，$f_n$ 的图像形成一个高为 $n$ 的等腰三角形，而当 $x\ge1/n$ 时，$f_n(x)=0$。这些函数可以显式定义如下：

blocks.source: $$f_n(x)=\begin{cases}2n^2x,&0\le x\le\dfrac1{2n}\\2n-2n^2x,&\dfrac1{2n}\le x\le\dfrac1n\\0,&\dfrac1n\le x\le1.\end{cases}$$

Because this sequence varies so erratically near $0$, our primitive mathematical instincts might suggest that $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ does not always exist. Nevertheless, this limit does exist for all $x$, and the function $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ is even continuous. In fact, if $x>0$, then $f_n(x)$ is eventually $0$, so $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=0$; moreover, $f_n(0)=0$ for all $n$, so that we certainly have $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(0)=0$. In other words, $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=0$ for all $x$. On the other hand, the integral quickly reveals the strange behavior of this sequence; we have
blocks.translation: 由于这个函数列在 $0$ 附近变化得如此不规则，我们朴素的数学直觉可能会认为 $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ 并不总是存在。然而，这个极限对所有 $x$ 都存在，而且函数 $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ 甚至是连续的。事实上，如果 $x>0$，那么 $f_n(x)$ 最终等于 $0$，所以 $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=0$；此外，对于所有 $n$ 都有 $f_n(0)=0$，因此当然有 $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(0)=0$。换句话说，对于所有 $x$，都有 $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=0$。另一方面，积分很快就揭示出这个函数列的奇特行为；我们有

blocks.source: but
blocks.translation: 但是

blocks.source: Thus,
blocks.translation: 因此，

blocks.source: $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_0^1f_n(x)\,dx\ne\int_0^1\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)\,dx.$$
This particular sequence of functions behaves in a way that we really never imagined when we first considered functions defined by limits. Although it is true that
blocks.translation: 这个特殊函数列的行为，是我们最初考虑通过极限定义函数时根本未曾想到的。虽然确实有

blocks.source: $$f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)\quad\text{for each }x\text{ in }[0,1],$$

the graphs of the functions $f_n$ do not “approach” the graph of $f$ in the sense of lying close to it—if, as in Figure 5, we draw a strip around $f$ of total width $2\varepsilon$ (allowing a width of $\varepsilon$ above and below), then the graphs of $f_n$ do not lie completely within this strip, no matter how large an $n$ we choose. Of course, for each $x$ there is some $N$ such that the point $(x,f_n(x))$ lies in this strip for $n>N$; this assertion just amounts to the fact that $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=f(x)$. But it is necessary to choose larger and larger $N$’s as $x$ is chosen closer and closer to $0$, and no one $N$ will work for all $x$ at once.
blocks.translation: 但函数 $f_n$ 的图像并没有在“靠近”的意义上“趋向”$f$ 的图像——如果像图 5 那样，在 $f$ 的图像周围画一条总宽度为 $2\varepsilon$ 的带状区域（上方和下方各留出 $\varepsilon$ 的宽度），那么无论选取多大的 $n$，$f_n$ 的图像都不会完全落在这个带状区域内。当然，对于每个 $x$，都存在某个 $N$，使得当 $n>N$ 时，点 $(x,f_n(x))$ 落在这个带状区域内；这句话恰好就是 $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)=f(x)$。但随着 $x$ 选得越来越接近 $0$，就必须选择越来越大的 $N$；不存在一个能同时适用于所有 $x$ 的 $N$。

blocks.source: The same situation actually occurs, though less blatantly, for each of the other examples given previously. Figure 6 illustrates this point for the sequence
blocks.translation: 实际上，先前给出的其他各个例子中也有同样的情况，只是没有这么明显。图 6 用下面这个函数列说明了这一点：

blocks.source: $$f_n(x)=\begin{cases}x^n,&0\le x\le1\\1,&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$

A strip of total width $2\varepsilon$ has been drawn around the graph of $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$. If $\varepsilon<\frac12$, this strip consists of two pieces, which contain no points with second
blocks.translation: 在 $f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)$ 的图像周围画出了总宽度为 $2\varepsilon$ 的带状区域。如果 $\varepsilon<\frac12$，这个区域由两部分组成，其中没有任何点的第二个

blocks.source: coordinate equal to $\frac12$; since each function $f_n$ takes on the value $\frac12$, the graph of each $f_n$ fails to lie within this strip. Once again, for each point $x$ there is some $N$ such that $(x,f_n(x))$ lies in the strip for $n>N$; but it is not possible to pick one $N$ which works for all $x$ at once.
blocks.translation: 坐标等于 $\frac12$；由于每个函数 $f_n$ 都取到值 $\frac12$，每个 $f_n$ 的图像都不完全位于这个带状区域内。同样，对于每个点 $x$，都存在某个 $N$，使得当 $n>N$ 时，$(x,f_n(x))$ 落在带状区域内；但是，不可能选出一个同时适用于所有 $x$ 的 $N$。

blocks.source: It is easy to check that precisely the same situation occurs for each of the other examples. In each case we have a function $f$, and a sequence of functions $\{f_n\}$, all defined on some set $A$, such that
blocks.translation: 很容易验证，其他各个例子也都出现完全相同的情况。在每个例子中，都有一个函数 $f$ 和一个函数列 $\{f_n\}$，它们全都定义在某个集合 $A$ 上，并且

blocks.source: $$f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)\quad\text{for all }x\text{ in }A.$$
This means that
blocks.translation: 这意味着

blocks.source: for all $\varepsilon>0$, and for all $x$ in $A$, there is some $N$ such that if $n>N$, then $|f(x)-f_n(x)|<\varepsilon$.
blocks.translation: 对于所有 $\varepsilon>0$，以及 $A$ 中的所有 $x$，都存在某个 $N$，使得如果 $n>N$，那么 $|f(x)-f_n(x)|<\varepsilon$。

blocks.source: But in each case different $N$’s must be chosen for different $x$’s, and in each case it is *not* true that
blocks.translation: 但是，在每个例子中，都必须针对不同的 $x$ 选择不同的 $N$；而且在每个例子中，下面的陈述都*不*成立：

blocks.source: for all $\varepsilon>0$ there is some $N$ such that for all $x$ in $A$, if $n>N$, then $|f(x)-f_n(x)|<\varepsilon$.
blocks.translation: 对于所有 $\varepsilon>0$，都存在某个 $N$，使得对于 $A$ 中的所有 $x$，如果 $n>N$，那么 $|f(x)-f_n(x)|<\varepsilon$。

blocks.source: Although this condition differs from the first only by a minor displacement of the phrase “for all $x$ in $A$,” it has a totally different significance. If a sequence $\{f_n\}$ satisfies this second condition, then the graphs of $f_n$ eventually lie close to the graph of $f$, as illustrated in Figure 7. This condition turns out to be just the one which makes the study of limit functions feasible.
blocks.translation: 虽然这个条件与第一个条件仅仅相差短语“对于 $A$ 中的所有 $x$”的位置略有移动，但它的意义完全不同。如果函数列 $\{f_n\}$ 满足第二个条件，那么 $f_n$ 的图像最终就会靠近 $f$ 的图像，如图 7 所示。事实证明，恰恰是这个条件使极限函数的研究成为可行。

blocks.source: ## DEFINITION
blocks.translation: ## 定义

blocks.source: Let $\{f_n\}$ be a sequence of functions defined on $A$, and let $f$ be a function which is also defined on $A$. Then $f$ is called the **uniform limit of $\{f_n\}$ on $A$** if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is some $N$ such that for all $x$ in $A$,
blocks.translation: 设 $\{f_n\}$ 是定义在 $A$ 上的函数列，$f$ 也是定义在 $A$ 上的函数。如果对于每个 $\varepsilon>0$，都存在某个 $N$，使得对于 $A$ 中的所有 $x$，都有下列关系，那么称 $f$ 为 **$\{f_n\}$ 在 $A$ 上的一致极限**：

blocks.source: $$\text{if }n>N,\text{ then }|f(x)-f_n(x)|<\varepsilon.$$
We also say that $\{f_n\}$ **converges uniformly to $f$ on $A$**, or that $f_n$ **approaches $f$ uniformly on $A$**.
blocks.translation: 我们也说，$\{f_n\}$ **在 $A$ 上一致收敛于 $f$**，或者 $f_n$ **在 $A$ 上一致趋近于 $f$**。

blocks.source: As a contrast to this definition, if we know only that
blocks.translation: 与这个定义相对，如果我们仅仅知道

blocks.source: $$f(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n(x)\quad\text{for each }x\text{ in }A,$$
then we say that $\{f_n\}$ **converges pointwise to $f$ on $A$**. Clearly, uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence (but not conversely!).
blocks.translation: 那么就说，$\{f_n\}$ **在 $A$ 上逐点收敛于 $f$**。显然，一致收敛蕴含逐点收敛（反过来却不成立！）。

blocks.source: Evidence for the usefulness of uniform convergence is not at all difficult to amass. Integrals represent a particularly easy topic; Figure 7 makes it almost obvious that if $\{f_n\}$ converges uniformly to $f$, then the integral of $f_n$ can be made as close to the integral of $f$ as desired. Expressed more precisely, we have the following theorem.
blocks.translation: 要积累一致收敛有用的证据，一点也不困难。积分是一个特别容易处理的话题；图 7 几乎显而易见地表明，如果 $\{f_n\}$ 一致收敛于 $f$，那么 $f_n$ 的积分可以任意接近 $f$ 的积分。更精确地说，我们有以下定理。

blocks.source: ## THEOREM 1
blocks.translation: ## 定理 1

blocks.source: Suppose that $\{f_n\}$ is a sequence of functions which are integrable on $[a,b]$, and that $\{f_n\}$ converges uniformly on $[a,b]$ to a function $f$ which is integrable on $[a,b]$. Then
blocks.translation: 假设 $\{f_n\}$ 是一列在 $[a,b]$ 上可积的函数，而且 $\{f_n\}$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上一致收敛于函数 $f$，后者在 $[a,b]$ 上可积。那么

blocks.source: $$\int_a^b f=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_a^b f_n.$$
## PROOF
blocks.translation: ## 证明

blocks.source: Let $\varepsilon>0$. There is some $N$ such that for all $n>N$ we have
blocks.translation: 设 $\varepsilon>0$。存在某个 $N$，使得对于所有 $n>N$，都有

blocks.source: $$|f(x)-f_n(x)|<\varepsilon\qquad\text{for all }x\text{ in }[a,b].$$
Thus, if $n>N$ we have
blocks.translation: 因此，如果 $n>N$，就有

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}\left|\int_a^bf(x)\,dx-\int_a^bf_n(x)\,dx\right|&=\left|\int_a^b[f(x)-f_n(x)]\,dx\right|\\&\le\int_a^b|f(x)-f_n(x)|\,dx\\&\le\int_a^b\varepsilon\,dx\\&=\varepsilon(b-a).\end{aligned}$$
Since this is true for any $\varepsilon>0$, it follows that
blocks.translation: 由于这对任意 $\varepsilon>0$ 都成立，所以

blocks.source: $$\int_a^b f=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_a^b f_n.\quad\blacksquare$$

The treatment of continuity is only a little bit more difficult, involving an “$\varepsilon/3$-argument,” a three-step estimate of $|f(x)-f(x+h)|$. If $\{f_n\}$ is a sequence of continuous functions which converges uniformly to $f$, then there is some $n$ such that
blocks.translation: 连续性的处理只稍微困难一些，需要一个“$\varepsilon/3$ 论证”，即分三步估计 $|f(x)-f(x+h)|$。如果 $\{f_n\}$ 是一个一致收敛于 $f$ 的连续函数列，那么存在某个 $n$，使得

blocks.source: $$|f(x)-f_n(x)|<\frac\varepsilon3,\tag{1}$$
$$|f(x+h)-f_n(x+h)|<\frac\varepsilon3.\tag{2}$$
Moreover, since $f_n$ is continuous, for sufficiently small $h$ we have
blocks.translation: 此外，由于 $f_n$ 连续，对于充分小的 $h$，有

blocks.source: $$|f_n(x)-f_n(x+h)|<\frac\varepsilon3.\tag{3}$$

It will follow from (1), (2), and (3) that $|f(x)-f(x+h)|<\varepsilon$. In order to obtain (3), however, we must restrict the size of $|h|$ in a way that cannot be predicted until $n$ has already been chosen; it is therefore quite essential that there be some fixed $n$ which makes (2) true, no matter how small $|h|$ may be—it is precisely at this point that uniform convergence enters the proof.
blocks.translation: 由 (1)、(2) 和 (3) 将得到 $|f(x)-f(x+h)|<\varepsilon$。不过，为了得到 (3)，我们必须限制 $|h|$ 的大小，而限制的具体方式在选定 $n$ 之前无法预知；因此，必须存在某个固定的 $n$，使得无论 $|h|$ 多么小，(2) 都成立——一致收敛恰恰是在这里进入证明的。

blocks.source: ## THEOREM 2
blocks.translation: ## 定理 2

blocks.source: Suppose that $\{f_n\}$ is a sequence of functions which are continuous on $[a,b]$, and that $\{f_n\}$ converges uniformly on $[a,b]$ to $f$. Then $f$ is also continuous on $[a,b]$.
blocks.translation: 假设 $\{f_n\}$ 是一列在 $[a,b]$ 上连续的函数，而且 $\{f_n\}$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上一致收敛于 $f$。那么 $f$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上也连续。

blocks.source: ## PROOF
blocks.translation: ## 证明

blocks.source: For each $x$ in $[a,b]$ we must prove that $f$ is continuous at $x$. We will deal only with $x$ in $(a,b)$; the cases $x=a$ and $x=b$ require the usual simple modifications.
blocks.translation: 对于 $[a,b]$ 中的每个 $x$，我们必须证明 $f$ 在 $x$ 处连续。我们只处理 $x$ 在 $(a,b)$ 中的情形；$x=a$ 和 $x=b$ 的情形只需作通常的简单修改。

blocks.source: Let $\varepsilon>0$. Since $\{f_n\}$ converges uniformly to $f$ on $[a,b]$, there is some $n$ such that
blocks.translation: 设 $\varepsilon>0$。由于 $\{f_n\}$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上一致收敛于 $f$，存在某个 $n$，使得

blocks.source: $$|f(y)-f_n(y)|<\frac\varepsilon3\quad\text{for all }y\text{ in }[a,b].$$
In particular, for all $h$ such that $x+h$ is in $[a,b]$, we have
blocks.translation: 特别地，对于所有使 $x+h$ 位于 $[a,b]$ 中的 $h$，都有

blocks.source: $$|f(x)-f_n(x)|<\frac\varepsilon3,\tag{1}$$
$$|f(x+h)-f_n(x+h)|<\frac\varepsilon3.\tag{2}$$
Now $f_n$ is continuous, so there is some $\delta>0$ such that for $|h|<\delta$ we have
blocks.translation: 现在，$f_n$ 连续，所以存在某个 $\delta>0$，使得当 $|h|<\delta$ 时有

blocks.source: $$|f_n(x)-f_n(x+h)|<\frac\varepsilon3.\tag{3}$$
Thus, if $|h|<\delta$, then
blocks.translation: 因此，如果 $|h|<\delta$，那么

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}&|f(x+h)-f(x)|\\&\quad=|f(x+h)-f_n(x+h)+f_n(x+h)-f_n(x)+f_n(x)-f(x)|\\&\quad\le|f(x+h)-f_n(x+h)|+|f_n(x+h)-f_n(x)|+|f_n(x)-f(x)|\\&\quad<\frac\varepsilon3+\frac\varepsilon3+\frac\varepsilon3\\&\quad=\varepsilon.\end{aligned}$$
This proves that $f$ is continuous at $x$. ■
blocks.translation: 这就证明了 $f$ 在 $x$ 处连续。■

blocks.source: After the two noteworthy successes provided by Theorem 1 and Theorem 2, the situation for differentiability turns out to be very disappointing. If each $f_n$ is differentiable, and if $\{f_n\}$ converges uniformly to $f$, it is still not necessarily true that $f$ is differentiable. For example, Figure 8 shows that there is a sequence of differentiable functions $\{f_n\}$ which converges uniformly to the function $f(x)=|x|$.
blocks.translation: 定理 1 和定理 2 带来了两次值得注意的成功，但可导性的情形却令人非常失望。即使每个 $f_n$ 都可导，而且 $\{f_n\}$ 一致收敛于 $f$，$f$ 仍然未必可导。例如，图 8 表明，存在一个可导函数列 $\{f_n\}$，一致收敛于函数 $f(x)=|x|$。

blocks.source: Even if $f$ is differentiable, it may not be true that
blocks.translation: 即使 $f$ 可导，也未必有

blocks.source: $$f'(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n'(x);$$
this is not at all surprising if we reflect that a smooth function can be approximated by very rapidly oscillating functions. For example (Figure 9), if
blocks.translation: 只要想到光滑函数也可以用振荡得非常快的函数逼近，这就一点也不令人意外了。例如（图 9），如果

blocks.source: $$f_n(x)=\frac1n\sin(n^2x),$$
then $\{f_n\}$ converges uniformly to the function $f(x)=0$, but
blocks.translation: 那么 $\{f_n\}$ 一致收敛于函数 $f(x)=0$，但是

blocks.source: Despite such examples, the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus practically guarantees that some sort of theorem about derivatives will be a consequence of Theorem 1; the crucial hypothesis is that $\{f_n'\}$ converges uniformly (to some continuous function).

blocks.source: ## THEOREM 3
blocks.translation: ## 定理 3

blocks.source: Suppose that $\{f_n\}$ is a sequence of functions which are differentiable on $[a,b]$, with integrable derivatives $f_n'$, and that $\{f_n\}$ converges (pointwise) to $f$. Suppose, moreover, that $\{f_n'\}$ converges uniformly on $[a,b]$ to some continuous function $g$. Then $f$ is differentiable and
blocks.translation: 假设 $\{f_n\}$ 是一列在 $[a,b]$ 上可导的函数，其导数 $f_n'$ 可积，而且 $\{f_n\}$（逐点）收敛于 $f$。再假设 $\{f_n'\}$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上一致收敛于某个连续函数 $g$。那么 $f$ 可导，并且

blocks.source: $$f'(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n'(x).$$
## PROOF
blocks.translation: ## 证明

blocks.source: Applying Theorem 1 to the interval $[a,x]$, we see that for each $x$ we have
blocks.translation: 把定理 1 应用于区间 $[a,x]$，可见对于每个 $x$，都有

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}\int_a^xg&=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_a^xf_n'\\&=\lim_{n\to\infty}[f_n(x)-f_n(a)]\\&=f(x)-f(a).\end{aligned}$$
Since $g$ is continuous, it follows that $f'(x)=g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n'(x)$ for all $x$ in the interval $[a,b]$. ■
blocks.translation: 由于 $g$ 连续，对于区间 $[a,b]$ 中的所有 $x$，都有 $f'(x)=g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n'(x)$。■

blocks.source: Now that the basic facts about uniform limits have been established, it is clear how to treat functions defined as infinite sums,
blocks.translation: 既然一致极限的基本事实已经建立，如何处理通过无穷和定义的函数也就清楚了：

our previous theorems apply when the new sequence

blocks.source: ## DEFINITION
blocks.translation: ## 定义

blocks.source: The series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ **converges uniformly** (more formally: the sequence $\{f_n\}$ is **uniformly summable**) **to $f$ on $A$**, if the sequence
blocks.translation: 如果下面的函数列一致收敛，就称级数 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ **在 $A$ 上一致收敛于 $f$**（更正式地说：数列 $\{f_n\}$ **一致可求和**）：

blocks.source: converges uniformly to $f$ on $A$.
blocks.translation: 这里，一致收敛是在 $A$ 上以 $f$ 为极限。

blocks.source: We can now apply each of Theorems 1, 2, and 3 to uniformly convergent series; the results may be stated in one common corollary.
blocks.translation: 现在，我们可以把定理 1、2、3 分别应用于一致收敛级数；所得结果可以合并为一个推论。

blocks.source: ## COROLLARY
blocks.translation: ## 推论

blocks.source: Let $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly to $f$ on $[a,b]$.
blocks.translation: 设 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上一致收敛于 $f$。

blocks.source: (1) If each $f_n$ is continuous on $[a,b]$, then $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$.
blocks.translation: (1) 如果每个 $f_n$ 都在 $[a,b]$ 上连续，那么 $f$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上连续。

blocks.source: (2) If $f$ and each $f_n$ is integrable on $[a,b]$, then
blocks.translation: (2) 如果 $f$ 及每个 $f_n$ 都在 $[a,b]$ 上可积，那么

blocks.source: $$\int_a^bf=\sum_{n=1}^\infty\int_a^bf_n.$$

Moreover, if $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ converges (pointwise) to $f$ on $[a,b]$, each $f_n$ has an integrable derivative $f_n'$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n'$ converges uniformly on $[a,b]$ to some continuous function, then
blocks.translation: 此外，如果 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上（逐点）收敛于 $f$，每个 $f_n$ 都有可积导数 $f_n'$，而且 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n'$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上一致收敛于某个连续函数，那么

blocks.source: $$(3)\quad f'(x)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n'(x)\qquad\text{for all }x\text{ in }[a,b].$$
## PROOF
blocks.translation: ## 证明

blocks.source: (1) If each $f_n$ is continuous, then so is each $f_1+\cdots+f_n$, and $f$ is the uniform limit of the sequence $f_1,\ f_1+f_2,\ f_1+f_2+f_3,\ \ldots$, so $f$ is continuous by Theorem 2.
blocks.translation: (1) 如果每个 $f_n$ 都连续，那么每个 $f_1+\cdots+f_n$ 也连续；而 $f$ 是函数列 $f_1,\ f_1+f_2,\ f_1+f_2+f_3,\ \ldots$ 的一致极限，所以根据定理 2，$f$ 连续。

blocks.source: (2) Since $f_1,\ f_1+f_2,\ f_1+f_2+f_3,\ \ldots$ converges uniformly to $f$, it follows from Theorem 1 that
blocks.translation: (2) 由于 $f_1,\ f_1+f_2,\ f_1+f_2+f_3,\ \ldots$ 一致收敛于 $f$，由定理 1 得到

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}\int_a^bf&=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_a^b(f_1+\cdots+f_n)\\&=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\int_a^bf_1+\cdots+\int_a^bf_n\right)\\&=\sum_{n=1}^\infty\int_a^bf_n.\end{aligned}$$

(3) Each function $f_1+\cdots+f_n$ is differentiable, with derivative $f_1'+\cdots+f_n'$, and $f_1',\ f_1'+f_2',\ f_1'+f_2'+f_3',\ \ldots$ converges uniformly to a continuous function, by hypothesis. It follows from Theorem 3 that
blocks.translation: (3) 每个函数 $f_1+\cdots+f_n$ 都可导，其导数为 $f_1'+\cdots+f_n'$；而根据假设，$f_1',\ f_1'+f_2',\ f_1'+f_2'+f_3',\ \ldots$ 一致收敛于一个连续函数。由定理 3 得到

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=\lim_{n\to\infty}[f_1'(x)+\cdots+f_n'(x)]\\&=\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n'(x).\quad\blacksquare\end{aligned}$$

At the moment this corollary is not very useful, since it seems quite difficult to predict when the sequence $f_1,\ f_1+f_2,\ f_1+f_2+f_3,\ldots$ will converge uniformly. The most important condition which ensures such uniform convergence is provided by the following theorem; the proof is almost a triviality because of the cleverness with which the very simple hypotheses have been chosen.
blocks.translation: 目前，这个推论还不太有用，因为要预先判断函数列 $f_1,\ f_1+f_2,\ f_1+f_2+f_3,\ldots$ 何时一致收敛，似乎相当困难。下面的定理给出了保证这种一致收敛的最重要条件；由于它巧妙地选取了非常简单的假设，其证明几乎轻而易举。

blocks.source: ## THEOREM 4 (THE WEIERSTRASS M-TEST)
blocks.translation: ## 定理 4（魏尔斯特拉斯 M 判别法）

blocks.source: Let $\{f_n\}$ be a sequence of functions defined on $A$, and suppose that $\{M_n\}$ is a sequence of numbers such that
blocks.translation: 设 $\{f_n\}$ 是定义在 $A$ 上的函数列，并假设 $\{M_n\}$ 是满足下列条件的数列：

blocks.source: $$|f_n(x)|\le M_n\qquad\text{for all }x\text{ in }A.$$

Suppose moreover that $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty M_n$ converges. Then for each $x$ in $A$ the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n(x)$ converges (in fact, it converges absolutely), and $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly on $A$ to the function
blocks.translation: 再假设 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty M_n$ 收敛。那么，对于 $A$ 中的每个 $x$，级数 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n(x)$ 都收敛（事实上，它绝对收敛），而且 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ 在 $A$ 上一致收敛于函数

blocks.source: $$f(x)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n(x).$$
## PROOF
blocks.translation: ## 证明

blocks.source: For each $x$ in $A$ the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty|f_n(x)|$ converges, by the comparison test; consequently $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n(x)$ converges (absolutely). Moreover, for all $x$ in $A$ we have
blocks.translation: 对于 $A$ 中的每个 $x$，根据比较判别法，级数 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty|f_n(x)|$ 收敛；因此 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n(x)$（绝对）收敛。此外，对于 $A$ 中的所有 $x$，有

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}\bigl|f(x)-[f_1(x)+\cdots+f_N(x)]\bigr|&=\left|\sum_{n=N+1}^\infty f_n(x)\right|\\&\le\sum_{n=N+1}^\infty|f_n(x)|\\&\le\sum_{n=N+1}^\infty M_n.\end{aligned}$$
Since $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty M_n$ converges, the number $\displaystyle\sum_{n=N+1}^\infty M_n$ can be made as small as desired, by choosing $N$ sufficiently large. ■
blocks.translation: 由于 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty M_n$ 收敛，只要选择充分大的 $N$，数 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=N+1}^\infty M_n$ 就可以任意小。■

blocks.source: $$\begin{aligned}|a_nx^n|&=|a_n|\cdot|x^n|\\&\le|a_n|\cdot|a^n|\\&=|a_n|\cdot|x_0|^n\cdot\left|\frac a{x_0}\right|^n\qquad\text{(this is the clever step)}\\&\le M\left|\frac a{x_0}\right|^n.\end{aligned}$$
But $|a/x_0|<1$, so the (geometric) series

$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac M{|a|}n\left|\frac a{x_0}\right|^n=\frac M{|a|}\sum_{n=1}^\infty n\left|\frac a{x_0}\right|^n$$

blocks.source: We are now in a position to manipulate power series with ease. Most algebraic manipulations are fairly straightforward consequences of general theorems about infinite series. For example, suppose that $f(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$ and $g(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_nx^n$, where the two power series both converge for some $x_0$. Then for $|x|<|x_0|$ we have
blocks.translation: 现在，我们已经能够自如地运算幂级数了。大多数代数运算，都是无穷级数一般定理相当直接的推论。例如，假设 $f(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$、$g(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_nx^n$，其中两个幂级数都在某个 $x_0$ 处收敛。那么，当 $|x|<|x_0|$ 时，有

blocks.source: $$\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n+\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_nx^n=\sum_{n=0}^\infty(a_nx^n+b_nx^n)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty(a_n+b_n)x^n.$$
So the series $h(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty(a_n+b_n)x^n$ also converges for $|x|<|x_0|$, and $h=f+g$ for these $x$.
blocks.translation: 所以级数 $h(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty(a_n+b_n)x^n$ 在 $|x|<|x_0|$ 时也收敛，而且对于这些 $x$，有 $h=f+g$。

blocks.source: Finally, suppose that $f(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$, where $a_0\ne0$, so that $f(0)=a_0\ne0$. Then we can try to find a power series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_nx^n$ which represents $1/f$. This means that we want to have

Since the left side of this equation will be given by the Cauchy product, we want to have

Since $a_0\ne0$, we can solve the first of these equations for $b_0$. Then we can solve the second for $b_1$, etc. Of course, we still have to prove that the new series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_nx^n$ does converge for some $x\ne0$. This is left as an exercise (Problem 18).

blocks.source: On this happy note we could easily end our study of power series and Taylor series. A careful assessment of our situation will reveal some unexplained facts, however.
blocks.translation: 我们完全可以带着这个令人愉快的结论，结束对幂级数与泰勒级数的研究。不过，仔细审视目前的状况，就会发现一些尚未解释的事实。

blocks.source: The Taylor series of $\sin$, $\cos$, and $\exp$ are as satisfactory as we could desire; they converge for all $x$, and can be differentiated term-by-term for all $x$. The Taylor series of the function $f(x)=\log(1+x)$ is slightly less pleasing, because it converges only for $-1<x\le1$, but this deficiency is a necessary consequence of the basic nature of power series. If the Taylor series for $f$ converged for any $x_0$ with $|x_0|>1$, then it would converge on the interval $(-|x_0|,|x_0|)$, and on this interval the function which it defines would be differentiable, and thus continuous. But this is impossible, since it is unbounded on the interval $(-1,1)$, where it equals $\log(1+x)$.
blocks.translation: $\sin$、$\cos$ 和 $\exp$ 的泰勒级数，令人满意得无以复加；它们对所有 $x$ 都收敛，也对所有 $x$ 都可以逐项求导。函数 $f(x)=\log(1+x)$ 的泰勒级数稍不那么令人满意，因为它只在 $-1<x\le1$ 时收敛；但这个缺陷是幂级数基本性质的必然结果。如果 $f$ 的泰勒级数在某个满足 $|x_0|>1$ 的 $x_0$ 处收敛，那么它就在区间 $(-|x_0|,|x_0|)$ 上收敛；在这个区间上，它定义的函数可导，因而连续。但这是不可能的，因为它在区间 $(-1,1)$ 上等于 $\log(1+x)$，而在那里无界。

blocks.source: The Taylor series for $\arctan$ is more difficult to comprehend—there seems to be no possible excuse for the refusal of this series to converge when $|x|>1$. This mysterious behavior is exemplified even more strikingly by the function $f(x)=1/(1+x^2)$, an infinitely differentiable function which is the next best thing to a polynomial function. blocks.source: If $|x|\ge1$ the Taylor series does not converge at all. Why? What unseen obstacle prevents the Taylor series from extending past $1$ and $-1$? Asking this sort of question is always dangerous, since we may have to settle for an unsympathetic answer: it happens because it happens—that’s the way things are! In this case there does happen to be an explanation, but this explanation is impossible to give at the present time; although the question is about real numbers, it can be answered intelligently only when placed in a broader context. It will therefore be necessary to devote two chapters to quite new material before completing our discussion of Taylor series in Chapter 27.
blocks.translation: 如果 $|x|\ge1$，泰勒级数根本不收敛。为什么？是什么看不见的障碍，阻止了泰勒级数越过 $1$ 和 $-1$？提出这类问题总是危险的，因为我们可能不得不接受一个毫不体贴的回答：发生了就是发生了——事情就是这样！在这个例子中，碰巧确实有一个解释，但目前还无法给出；虽然问题涉及实数，却只有把它放进一个更广阔的背景，才能给出有意义的回答。因此，在第 27 章完成对泰勒级数的讨论之前，我们需要用两章来研究全新的内容。

blocks.source: Suppose that $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n$ converges. We know that the series $f(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$ must converge uniformly on $[-a,a]$ for $0<a<1$, but it may not converge uniformly on $[-1,1]$; in fact, it may not even converge at the point $-1$ (for example, if $f(x)=\log(1+x)$). However, a beautiful theorem of Abel shows that the series *does* converge uniformly on $[0,1]$. Consequently, $f$ is continuous on $[0,1]$, and in particular, $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n=\lim_{x\to1^-}\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$. Prove Abel’s Theorem by noticing that if $|a_m+\cdots+a_n|<\varepsilon$, then $|a_mx^m+\cdots+a_nx^n|<\varepsilon$, by Abel’s Lemma (Problem 19-36).
blocks.translation: 假设 $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n$ 收敛。我们知道，级数 $f(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$ 对于 $0<a<1$ 必定在 $[-a,a]$ 上一致收敛，但它未必在 $[-1,1]$ 上一致收敛；事实上，它甚至可能在点 $-1$ 处不收敛（例如 $f(x)=\log(1+x)$ 时）。然而，阿贝尔的一个优美定理表明，这个级数*确实*在 $[0,1]$ 上一致收敛。因此，$f$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上连续，特别地，$\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n=\lim_{x\to1^-}\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$。证明阿贝尔定理，方法是注意到：根据阿贝尔引理（习题 19-36），如果 $|a_m+\cdots+a_n|<\varepsilon$，那么 $|a_mx^m+\cdots+a_nx^n|<\varepsilon$。

blocks.source: A sequence $\{a_n\}$ is called **Abel summable** if $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1^-}\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$ exists; Problem 19 shows that a summable sequence is necessarily Abel summable. Hint: Look over the list of Taylor series until you find one which does not converge at $1$, even though the function it represents is continuous at $1$.
blocks.translation: 如果 $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1^-}\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$ 存在，就称数列 $\{a_n\}$ **阿贝尔可求和**；习题 19 表明，可求和数列必定阿贝尔可求和。找一个阿贝尔可求和、但不可求和的数列。提示：查看泰勒级数表，找出一个在 $1$ 处不收敛、但它所表示的函数在 $1$ 处连续的级数。

blocks.translation: (c) 如果 $f$ 不连续，迪尼定理还成立吗？如果把 $[a,b]$ 换成开区间 $(a,b)$，又如何？

blocks.source: (a) Suppose that $\{f_n\}$ is a sequence of continuous functions on $[a,b]$ that converges uniformly to $f$. Prove that if $x_n$ approaches $x$, then $f_n(x_n)$ approaches $f(x)$.
blocks.translation: (a) 假设 $\{f_n\}$ 是 $[a,b]$ 上的连续函数列，一致收敛于 $f$。证明：如果 $x_n$ 趋于 $x$，那么 $f_n(x_n)$ 趋于 $f(x)$。

blocks.source: (b) Is this statement true without assuming that the $f_n$ are continuous?
blocks.translation: (b) 如果不假设各个 $f_n$ 连续，这个陈述还成立吗？

blocks.source: (c) Prove the converse of part (a): If $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and $\{f_n\}$ is a sequence with the property that $f_n(x_n)$ approaches $f(x)$ whenever $x_n$ approaches $x$, then $f_n$ converges uniformly to $f$ on $[a,b]$. Hint: If not, there is an $\varepsilon>0$ and a sequence $x_n$ with $|f_n(x_n)-f(x_n)|>\varepsilon$ for infinitely many distinct $x_n$. Then use the Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem.
blocks.translation: (c) 证明 (a) 的逆命题：如果 $f$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上连续，而函数列 $\{f_n\}$ 具有这样的性质——每当 $x_n$ 趋于 $x$ 时，$f_n(x_n)$ 就趋于 $f(x)$——那么 $f_n$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上一致收敛于 $f$。提示：否则，就存在一个 $\varepsilon>0$ 和一个数列 $x_n$，使无穷多个互不相同的 $x_n$ 满足 $|f_n(x_n)-f(x_n)|>\varepsilon$。然后使用博尔查诺–魏尔斯特拉斯定理。

blocks.source: This problem outlines a completely different approach to the integral; consequently, it is unfair to use any facts about integrals learned previously.
blocks.translation: 本题概述一种完全不同的积分处理方法；因此，使用先前学过的任何积分事实，都不算公平。

blocks.source: (a) Let $s$ be a step function on $[a,b]$, so that $s$ is constant on $(t_{i-1},t_i)$ for some partition $\{t_0,\ldots,t_n\}$ of $[a,b]$. Define $\displaystyle\int_a^b s$ as $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\cdot(t_i-t_{i-1})$ where $s_i$ is the (constant) value of $s$ on $(t_{i-1},t_i)$. Show that this definition does not depend on the partition $\{t_0,\ldots,t_n\}$.
blocks.translation: (a) 设 $s$ 是 $[a,b]$ 上的阶梯函数，因此对于 $[a,b]$ 的某个分割 $\{t_0,\ldots,t_n\}$，$s$ 在 $(t_{i-1},t_i)$ 上为常数。把 $\displaystyle\int_a^b s$ 定义为 $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\cdot(t_i-t_{i-1})$，其中 $s_i$ 是 $s$ 在 $(t_{i-1},t_i)$ 上的（常数）值。证明这个定义不依赖于分割 $\{t_0,\ldots,t_n\}$。

blocks.source: (b) A function $f$ is called a **regulated** function on $[a,b]$ if it is the uniform limit of a sequence of step functions $\{s_n\}$ on $[a,b]$. Show that in this case there is, for every $\varepsilon>0$, some $N$ such that for $m,n>N$ we have $|s_n(x)-s_m(x)|<\varepsilon$ for all $x$ in $[a,b]$.
blocks.translation: (b) 如果函数 $f$ 是 $[a,b]$ 上某个阶梯函数列 $\{s_n\}$ 的一致极限，就称它是 $[a,b]$ 上的**有规函数**。证明在这种情况下，对于每个 $\varepsilon>0$，都存在某个 $N$，使得当 $m,n>N$ 时，对于 $[a,b]$ 中的所有 $x$，都有 $|s_n(x)-s_m(x)|<\varepsilon$。

blocks.source: (c) Show that the sequence of numbers $\displaystyle\left\{\int_a^b s_n\right\}$ will be a Cauchy sequence.
blocks.translation: (c) 证明数列 $\displaystyle\left\{\int_a^b s_n\right\}$ 是一个柯西数列。

blocks.source: (d) Suppose that $\{t_n\}$ is another sequence of step functions on $[a,b]$ which converges uniformly to $f$. Show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is an $N$ such that for $n>N$ we have $|s_n(x)-t_n(x)|<\varepsilon$ for $x$ in $[a,b]$.
blocks.translation: (d) 假设 $\{t_n\}$ 是 $[a,b]$ 上另一个一致收敛于 $f$ 的阶梯函数列。证明：对于每个 $\varepsilon>0$，都存在一个 $N$，使得当 $n>N$ 时，对于 $[a,b]$ 中的 $x$，都有 $|s_n(x)-t_n(x)|<\varepsilon$。

blocks.source: (e) Conclude that $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_a^b s_n=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_a^b t_n$. This means that we can *define* $\displaystyle\int_a^b f$ to be $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}s_n$ for any sequence of step functions $\{s_n\}$ converging uniformly to $f$. The only remaining question is: Which functions are regulated?
blocks.translation: (e) 由此得出 $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_a^b s_n=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_a^b t_n$。这意味着，对于任意一个一致收敛于 $f$ 的阶梯函数列 $\{s_n\}$，我们都可以把 $\displaystyle\int_a^b f$ *定义*为 $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}s_n$。唯一剩下的问题是：哪些函数是有规函数？

blocks.source: \*(f) Prove that a continuous function is regulated. Hint: To find a step function $s$ on $[a,b]$ with $|f(x)-s(x)|<\varepsilon$ for all $x$ in $[a,b]$, consider all $y$ for which there is such a step function on $[a,y]$.
blocks.translation: \*(f) 证明连续函数是有规函数。提示：要在 $[a,b]$ 上找到一个阶梯函数 $s$，使得对于 $[a,b]$ 中的所有 $x$ 都有 $|f(x)-s(x)|<\varepsilon$，可以考虑所有这样的 $y$：在 $[a,y]$ 上存在满足要求的阶梯函数。

blocks.source: (g) Every step function $s$ has the property that $\lim_{x\to a^+}s(x)$ and $\lim_{x\to a^-}s(x)$ exist for all $a$. Conclude that every regulated function has the same property, and find an integrable function that is not regulated. (It is also true that, conversely, every function $f$ with the property that $\lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)$ and $\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x)$ exist for all $a$ is regulated.)
blocks.translation: (g) 每个阶梯函数 $s$ 都具有如下性质：对于所有 $a$，$\lim_{x\to a^+}s(x)$ 和 $\lim_{x\to a^-}s(x)$ 都存在。由此得出，每个有规函数也具有相同性质，并找一个可积但不是有规函数的例子。（反过来也成立：每个函数 $f$，只要对于所有 $a$，$\lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)$ 和 $\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x)$ 都存在，就必定是有规函数。）

blocks.source: Find a sequence $\{f_n\}$ approaching $f$ uniformly on $[0,1]$ for which we have $\lim_{n\to\infty}$ (length of $f_n$ on $[0,1]$) $\ne$ length of $f$ on $[0,1]$. (Length is defined in Problem 13-25, but the simplest example will involve functions the length of whose graphs will be obvious.)
blocks.translation: 找一个在 $[0,1]$ 上一致趋于 $f$ 的函数列 $\{f_n\}$，使得 $\lim_{n\to\infty}$（$f_n$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上的长度）$\ne$ $f$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上的长度。（长度在习题 13-25 中定义，但最简单的例子会涉及图像长度显而易见的函数。）
